rv.q: The result is harrowing but also deeply humane, a piece of theater whose darkness makes its flashes of beauty all the more affecting.
It is evocative, satisfying, and memorable theater.
The House of the Negro Insane is that most devilish thing, a play that is just good enough to make one wish it was so very much better.
The actors did the best they could with the material.
Terence Anthony's The House of the Negro Insane...is a searing drama about confinement, despair, and the possibility of freedom.

cn.t: Anthony's searing drama about a 1935 Jim Crow-era psychiatric institution earns praise for its evocative exploration of a dark chapter in history, though execution proves uneven. Critics find it largely compelling despite flaws.
